summary: Saskatchewan steel fire tower near the Torch River, built in 1938 and later dismantled; the site is now a fire cache, per a 2009 local history.

facts.status_note: No tower stands. The old tower yard is now the Grassy Lake Fire Cache, per a 2009 local history.

events.note: Third Grassy Lake tower, the first all-steel one, two miles north of the Torch River School
The new tower was first manned in 1938
A new cupola was put on the tower
Grassy Lake field office closed; the article ties this to the office, not the tower
Forest fire burned most of that summer north of Torch River and Moose Run; Syd Stubbington was the officer in charge
Tower completely overhauled, per the DNR annual report for 1963-64
Walter Kratz, towerman through most of the tower's years, retired; the article does not say who staffed the tower afterwards
New steel tower put into service about five miles north; third tower served until 1973; old tower decommissioned and eventually dismantled. The 2009 article also gives 1971 for the new tower

notes_for_editor: Replacement-tower date conflicts. The Website Service listing and the 2009 article's footnote say about 1971 (the article's footnote says 'built in 1971'); the 2009 article's main text says a new tower went into service in 1974. Event recorded as 1974 with the 1971 date in the note. Tower identity in the listing is unclear: its height (105 ft) and 1954 cupola are not tied to a specific structure. Brief lists the agency as Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency; none of the three sources names SPSA. They name the DNR, and the 2009 article's text names Saskatchewan Environment and Resource Management (SERM) in the Website Service page. Walter Kratz also appears as Kraatz and Krantz in the sources. Present-day status and access are not verified; the newest source is from 2009. No photos added.
